_roadWidth: MEASURED off the painted lane, not assumed: the median clearance from the cyan centre stroke to the nearest pixel that is not road, doubled. Narrowest 22.2 and widest 46.2 canvas px on the half-width; the median is the honest number because the lane has to fit its narrowest stretch. Level 1's road is 80.0, so this one is 18% tighter and every lateral figure derived from it moves with it.
note: EVERY NUMBER HERE IS DERIVED FROM tools/level2_path_overlay.png, which is the volcanic plate with the lane's centre stroked in cyan and seventeen candidate tower pads ringed and numbered in green. That is the difference from level 1: this plate came with its route drawn on it, so nothing here is a classifier's guess about what is road. Re-derive with `python3 tools/check_level2.py --emit` after any re-export, and check the stored file against the art with `python3 tools/check_level2.py`. The overlay lives under tools/ and NOT under public/, because everything in public/ is deployed whether or not anything references it and this is 1.9MB that only that one script opens.
_waypoints: Douglas-Peucker at 1.1 overlay px over the traced centre of the cyan stroke. MEASURED, not asserted: check_level2.py walks the painted centreline and reports the worst distance from it to this polyline, and that number is 1.0 OVERLAY px (0.9 canvas px) against a stroke four px wide, so the route is inside the paint for its whole length. The note used to claim 0.6, which was a number from an earlier epsilon that nothing re-measured after the epsilon moved — a file documenting a figure its own check disagreed with. THE TWO END POINTS ARE EXTENSIONS, NOT TRACED: enemies walk in from off the plate at x=-60 and out at x=1340, and each of those is a new point on the line the lane is already travelling when it reaches the edge. Level 1 drags its end waypoints out to those x values in place, which is free on that plate because its lane meets both edges flat. This lane arrives on a slope, and the same drag swung the opening segment 13 overlay px off the paint.
_buildSpots: FIFTEEN PADS FROM SEVENTEEN PAINTED RINGS. The overlay rings and numbers seventeen candidate spots; two of them are deliberately not pads and check_level2.py prints them on every run rather than failing, because which candidates become pads is a design decision the art cannot record. The two are the ring at 0.054,0.356 — canvas (69.3, 256.0), 69 px from the left edge and inside the stretch where enemies are still fading in off the plate — and the ring at 0.385,0.948 — canvas (493.3, 682.7), 36 px from the bottom edge, closer than the pad plate's own half-width of 39.7 world px, so its dirt oval would hang off the painting. Every other ring clears every edge by at least 79 px. Order is the overlay's reading order, top to bottom, and carries no meaning. SPACING IS THE ART'S, AND IT IS TIGHT. The rings are drawn about 15 world px across and the game gives a node a 34 px tap radius, so the painter's spacing is not the game's: pads 2-5 sit 59.0 px apart and 5-7 sit 59.6, both inside two tap radii, and 5-6 clear them by 1.3. Level 1's closest pair is 186.3, held there by a 141 px minimum in the tracer. Two overlapping pairs of tap targets have to be resolved before anyone plays this map, and they are resolved by moving a ring in the overlay, not by editing this file. check_level2.py prints every offending pair on each run.
_heroStart: MEASURED AGAINST THE PAINTED PLATE WITH THE SPRITE'S REAL HEIGHT, not derived from clearances alone. He is about 120 world px tall, and the value this replaces — (588.0, 128.0) — put his feet at y=128, which is above the lane's own highest point of 163.7: his head was over the top edge of the board and his footprint was in a lava field, 129 px of it. This position was chosen by requiring his whole 120x55 footprint to be clear of molten rock and then keeping the clearances that made the old spot look reasonable. What it measures: 0 lava pixels under him and 109.3 px to the nearest lava, 94.2 px from the road's edge, and 78.9 px from the nearest pad. Re-check with `python3 tools/check_level2.py`.
